intro.title: Incident Response & Reliability
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simulated incident response dashboard that monitors system health and triggers alerts. You will learn the core concepts of incident response workflows, including error detection, alerting, and status communication. The main technologies involved are state management for tracking incidents and event handlers for simulating system failures and recoveries. This hands-on project will help you understand how to maintain reliability by quickly identifying and addressing issues in a production environment.
intro.usecase: Incident response and reliability engineering are critical in production systems like cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure) or SaaS applications (e.g., Slack, GitHub). Developers implement real-time monitoring dashboards that display system health metrics, error rates, and incident alerts, enabling rapid diagnosis. For example, a reliability dashboard might feature panels showing service uptime, latency graphs, and automated incident ticketing forms to log and track outages. This pattern ensures teams can quickly detect, respond to, and resolve issues, maintaining high availability and user trust in live products.
